subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: Should explicit `pty:true` in sandboxed exec warn and continue without PTY, fail closed, or be held for backend-supported sandbox PTY behavior?
rationale: The source-level issue is clear, but the answer defines user-visible behavior at a sandbox execution boundary and should reflect maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning plus docs and tests that `pty:true` is ignored in sandbox mode.

options.title: Fail Closed
options.body: Reject explicit sandboxed PTY requests so callers cannot mistake pipe execution for a terminal session.

options.title: Design Sandbox PTY Support
options.body: Keep this open for a broader backend-specific PTY design rather than only documenting the current downgrade.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning plus docs and tests that `pty:true` is ignored in sandbox mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The original exec PTY behavior and docs trace to this owner signal, making it the best available routing candidate for the contract choice.
